chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man from his companions, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'My servants have not drawn closer to Me with anything more beloved to Me than three characteristics.' Musa said: 'O Lord, and what are they?' He said: 'O Musa, asceticism in the world, and piety from disobediences, and weeping from My fear.'

Musa said: 'O Lord, so what is for the one who does that?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Musa! As for those ascetic in the world, they are in Paradise; and as for those weeping from My fear, they are in the Lofty Highest, no one shares with them; and as for those pious from My disobediences, I examine the people and do not examine them.'

key_terms.أُفَتِّشُ: I examine/scrutinize (referring to the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.الرَّفِيعُ الْأَعْلَى: The Lofty Highest, a high rank in Paradise
key_terms.الزُّهْدُ: Asceticism or detachment from worldly desires
key_terms.الْوَرَعُ: Piety or caution regarding sins and doubtful matters

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics most beloved to God for drawing closer to Him, and what are their respective rewards?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys a divine message to Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) identifying asceticism (*zuhd*), piety (*wara'*), and weeping from fear (*bukaa'*) as the most beloved acts of worship to God. The text distinguishes the rewards for each: ascetics enter Paradise, those who weep from fear attain the exclusive highest ranks (*al-rafi' al-a'la*), and the pious are spared from detailed scrutiny on the Day of Judgment. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on inner emotional states, particularly weeping, as a direct path to spiritual elevation and divine intimacy.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from a man from our companions who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Musa<sup>as</sup>: “My<sup>azwj</sup> servants would not (be able to) come closer to Me<sup>azwj</sup> with anything more Beloved to Me<sup>azwj</sup> than three characteritics”. Musa<sup>as</sup> said: ‘And what are these?’ He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “O Musa<sup>as</sup>! (These are) the asceticism (avoiding indulgence) in the world, and the piety from the disobedience, and the weeping from My<sup>azwj</sup> fear”.

Musa<sup>as</sup>! O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! So what is for the one who does that?’ So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “O Musa<sup>as</sup>! As for the ascetic ones in the world, so they would be in the Paradise; and as for ones weeping from My<sup>azwj</sup> fear, so they would be in the lofty positions, no one would be participating with them; and as for the ones pious from My<sup>azwj</sup> disobedience, so I<sup>azwj</sup> will be Examining the people and would not be Examining them”’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from a man from certain individuals of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, sent revelations to Moses that said, “the most beloved of things to Me with which My servants can seek nearness to Me are three things.” Moses then asked, ‘Lord, what are they?’ The Lord said, ‘One’s reduced interest in worldly matters, restraint from sins and weeping for fear of Me.’

Moses asked, ‘Lord, what is then the reward for one who would do so?’ Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, sent him revelation that said, ‘Moses, people with reduced interest in the world will be in paradise, those weeping for fear of Me will be in a high position with whom no one else will share and those restraining from sins for their reward will have the privilege of freedom from My searching their affairs when I search all other people.’”
